paper.title: An Asymptotically Optimal Policy for Finite Support Models in the Multiarmed Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with finite support model A (distributions with finite support in known [a,b])
unmapped: reward distributions have finite (but unknown) support contained in a known bounded interval [a,b] (normalized to [-1,0])
settings.definition_quote: Let $\fb\equiv\{F:|\supp(F)|<\infty,\,\supp(F)\subset [a,b]\}$ be the family of distributions with a {\em finite} bounded support, where $\supp(F)$ is the support of distribution $F$ and $a,b$ are constants known to the player. We assume $a=-1,\,b=0$ without loss of generality.

symbols.c_0: term bounded by a constant independent of N (the O(1) term, depending on F and eps)

conditions: unique optimal arm j; bound is for each suboptimal arm i
reward distributions have finite support in [-1,0] (known bounds)

source.label: optMD
source.quote: Fix $\bm{F}\in\fb^K$ satisfying $\mu_j=\mu^*$ and $\mu_i<\mu^*$ for all $i\neq j$. Under MED policy, for any $i\neq j$ and $\ep>0$ it holds that \E_{\bm{F}}[T_i(N)]\le \frac{1+\ep}{\dmin(F_i,\mu^*,\fb)}\log N +\lo(1).

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of suboptimal arm i (quantity 'other'); D_min(F_i,mu*,A) equals D_inf (Lemma 2), i.e. Kinf_i for the finite-support model. Implies limsup E[T_i(N)]/log N <= 1/Kinf_i, matching the Burnetas-Katehakis lower bound (asymptotic optimality). The O(1) term encoded as c_0.

source.label: optMD
source.quote: Note that we obtain $$\limsup_{N\to\infty} \frac{\E_{\bm{F}}[T_i(N)]}{\log N} \le \frac{1}{\dmin(F_i,\mu^*,\fb)},$$ by dividing both sides by $\log N$, letting $N\to\infty$ and finally letting $\epsilon \downarrow 0$.

results.notes: Direct asymptotic consequence of Theorem 3 stated in the text; per-arm pull count. Corollary 1 gives weaker bound with D_min over A_X for any known support X containing 0 (generalizing Burnetas-Katehakis); not recorded separately.

cited_results.cited_title: Optimal adaptive policies for sequential allocation problems
cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit with general model F, consistent policies; lower bound on expected number of pulls of inferior arm i
